run.question: Our analytics dashboard seems slow. Can you check the shard configuration for the app-186-shard-analytics index? How many primary shards does it have and what is their status?

report.summary: Shard-configuration question is answered: app-186-shard-analytics has 7 primary shards and 0 replicas; all 7 primaries (shard 0 through 6) are STARTED on the single node bea971fdc0c6 (172.17.0.2), and the index reports health green with no unassigned, relocating or initializing shards at query time. The index holds 1 document (store ~6.1 kB), so 7 shards is over-sharded for its data volume and is also the only app-186 index with 7 shards — the 100 app-186-shard-data-001..100 indices each have 5. That does not by itself explain dashboard slowness: at the sampled instant the node shows heap 49%, CPU 12%, 104 GB free of 160 GB disk, and zero rejections in the search and write thread pools. The cluster carries 510 primary shards on one node with a 2 GiB heap (~255 shards per GB), which is a plausible contributor to query latency but was not measured. I found no measured latency signal for this index or for a dashboard service, so the slowness cause remains unresolved rather than identified. No root cause is named.

claims.text: Index app-186-shard-analytics reports pri=7, rep=0, health green, status open, docs.count=1 and store.size 1.5kb in the index listing.

All 7 primary shards of app-186-shard-analytics (shard 0,1,2,3,4,5,6) have state STARTED, are of type p (primary, no replica rows), and are all allocated on node bea971fdc0c6 at ip 172.17.0.2; shard 0 holds 1 document and shards 1-6 hold 0.

Cluster health at index level shows for app-186-shard-analytics: number_of_shards 7, number_of_replicas 0, active_primary_shards 7, active_shards 7, unassigned_shards 0, unassigned_primary_shards 0, relocating_shards 0, initializing_shards 0, status green.

The cluster docker-cluster has number_of_nodes 1 and number_of_data_nodes 1, 510 active primary shards and 510 active shards with 0 unassigned, 0 relocating, 0 initializing and overall status green; the other workload indices app-186-shard-data-001 through app-186-shard-data-100 each have number_of_shards 5 and number_of_replicas 0, while .security-7 and two .ds-* indices have 1 shard each.

Index stats for app-186-shard-analytics show docs.count 1, indexing.index_total 1 with index_failed 0, search.query_total 0, search.fetch_total 0, search.query_failure 0, refresh.total 15, 1 segment and store size_in_bytes 6143 (cumulative counters, not window deltas).

The single node bea971fdc0c6 (roles include data, master, ingest) shows jvm heap_used_percent 49 (heap_max 2 GiB), os.cpu.percent 12 with load_average 1m 1.48 / 5m 2.05, filesystem 104036843520 bytes free of 160497381376, thread_pool search rejected 0 / queue 0 and write rejected 0 / queue 0.

Over-sharding may contribute to dashboard slowness: app-186-shard-analytics spreads 1 document across 7 primary shards (its sibling indices use 5), and the whole cluster runs 510 primary shards on one data node with a 2 GiB heap (~255 shards per GB), so each dashboard search fans out across many shard-level search contexts. This is a plausible contributor only; no query latency for this index or for a dashboard service was measured.

Nothing at the sampled instant shows shard-related resource saturation or allocation failure: no unassigned/relocating/initializing shards cluster-wide, index green, node CPU 12%, heap 49%, disk 65% free, and zero search and write thread-pool rejections or queued tasks.

Cumulative index stats for app-186-shard-analytics report search.query_total 0 and fetch_total 0, so these counters show no searches counted against this index since the stats were reset; this does not show the dashboard avoids the index, since counters are cumulative and not scoped to the incident window.

Review whether the analytics dashboard actually queries app-186-shard-analytics or the app-186-shard-data-* indices, and compare the index/template number_of_shards setting that produced 7 shards for this index against the 5 used by its siblings; if the 510-shards-per-node ratio is confirmed as a latency factor, reduce shard count (shrink/ILM or fewer shards per index) before assuming the shard layout is the cause of slowness.

gaps: No query-latency or search-duration signal for app-186-shard-analytics (or for any dashboard service) was measured; search.query_time_in_millis for this index is 0 in cumulative stats, so slowness is unquantified.

All Elasticsearch state read here (index list, _cat/shards, cluster health, index stats, node stats) describes the cluster at query time 2026-11-23T17:37 and cannot show shard allocation or health during the incident window inside 2026-10-24..2026-11-23.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so when or by which change the 7-shard configuration was applied could not be verified.

Index settings (number_of_shards template, routing, ILM) cannot be read directly with the available tools; the 7 shards are known only from pri/shard listings, and any shard-count rationale or template is unknown.
Whether the slow dashboard is served by a Kubernetes workload that queries this index was not established: no service-to-index mapping, logs or traces were examined for this question.
search.query_total 0 is a cumulative counter that shows only what was counted since the last stats reset; it is not evidence of query volume, or its absence, during the incident window.
